text:
B: So, er, we just talk then, is it?
A: Yeah, think so. Three minutes.
B: Right. Where are you, then?
A: Normanton. Near Wakefield.
B: Yorkshire. I'm Dagenham. East London.
A: Yeah.
B: What d'you do?
A: Warehouse. Picking, like. Part-time, mostly lates, at a distribution centre off the M62. I'm knackered to be honest, did one last night and the heating's broke again, so you're freezing for eight hours.
B: I did warehouse when I was a kid. YTS. Didn't stick it.
A: Ha. It's alright. Pays for my stuff, do you know what I mean. You?
B: Office at a skip firm in Rainham. Phones, booking skips in, chasing people what ain't paid. My back went so they stuck me indoors. Can't complain. Well, I can. I do.
A: Sounds alright, that. Kettle on all day.
B: Kettle's the best bit of the job, mate.
A: Yeah.
B: You do a lot of these, then? Studies and that.
A: Yeah, loads. Surveys, cashback apps, all sorts. Do you know when this one pays out, actually?
B: No idea. Tracey reckons I'm addicted to 'em. The surveys.
A: I do trainers as well. Vinted, eBay. Sold a pair of Jordans last week for double what I paid. You just sort of look for people who don't know what they've got, like they've listed it wrong or the photos are rubbish, and you get in quick before anyone else does. Do you know what I mean.
B: Marketplace, me. Tools, mostly. Had a bloke last week try and mug me off on a drill, wanted forty quid for something half knackered. Got him down to fifteen.
A: Nice. Haggling's half of it.
B: Half of it. Other half's not getting done over yourself.
A: Yeah.
B: That a rugby scarf behind you?
A: Trinity. Wakefield Trinity, rugby league. They were rubbish at the weekend, so.
B: West Ham. Don't get me started. Gave my season ticket up when they moved to that soulless bowl. Watch it on the laptop now.
A: I'm not really fussed about football unless I've got an accumulator on. Lost it on the last game, as per.
B: Always the last game. I do the odd one Saturday. Scratchcards. Never win nothing.
A: Little laugh. Yeah.
B: My son's called Liam, funny enough. Twenty-six. Moved out to Romford with his girlfriend.
A: Yeah? I'm still at my mum's, so. Thirty and in the box room.
B: Nothing wrong with that. Rents round mine are a joke. Can't get a flat for under a grand.
A: Same up here, sort of. Not that bad, but still.
B: He don't ring much, mine. Once they're gone, they're gone.
A: Yeah, I should prob ring my dad more, to be fair, he's only in Ponte, I just—
